# JSON Patch

> [JSON Patch][json-patch] ([RFC 6902][rfc-6902]) utilities for applying operations to JSON documents immutably.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var jsonpatch = require( '@stdlib/utils/json-patch' );
```

The namespace exports the following:

-   **jsonpatch.apply( document, operations )**: apply a full patch array atomically.
-   **jsonpatch.validate( operations )**: validate a patch operations array structure.
-   **jsonpatch.add( document, path, value )**: apply a single `add` operation.
-   **jsonpatch.remove( document, path )**: apply a single `remove` operation.
-   **jsonpatch.replace( document, path, value )**: apply a single `replace` operation.
-   **jsonpatch.move( document, from, path )**: apply a single `move` operation.
-   **jsonpatch.copy( document, from, path )**: apply a single `copy` operation.
-   **jsonpatch.test( document, path, value )**: test whether a value at a path equals an expected value.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   All operations are **immutable** — the original document is never modified. Instead, a new document is returned using structural sharing (only objects along the modified path are cloned).
-   The `apply` function provides **atomicity** — if any operation in the patch array fails, none of the operations take effect.
-   All JSON Pointer paths are validated against prototype pollution vectors (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`).
-   Implements all six operations defined in [RFC 6902][rfc-6902]: `add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy`, and `test`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

## Examples

```javascript
var jsonpatch = require( '@stdlib/utils/json-patch' );

// Apply a full patch:
var doc = {
    'title': 'My Chart',
    'data': {
        'values': [ 1, 2, 3 ]
    }
};
var ops = [
    { 'op': 'replace', 'path': '/title', 'value': 'Updated Chart' },
    { 'op': 'add', 'path': '/data/values/-', 'value': 4 },
    { 'op': 'remove', 'path': '/data/values/0' }
];
var result = jsonpatch.apply( doc, ops );
// result => { 'title': 'Updated Chart', 'data': { 'values': [ 2, 3, 4 ] } }

// Original is untouched:
// doc.title => 'My Chart'
// doc.data.values => [ 1, 2, 3 ]

// Use individual operations:
var doc2 = { 'foo': [ 1, 2, 3 ] };
var out = jsonpatch.add( doc2, '/foo/-', 4 );
// out.foo => [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]

// Validate before applying:
var err = jsonpatch.validate( [ { 'op': 'add', 'path': '/foo' } ] );
// err => <Error> (missing 'value')
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->
